verdict.rationale: Sill's own Remote Access feature lets you use your Mac away from home through your own VPN (Tailscale is named) or a port forwarded on your router. It also adapts quality for slower links when away and moves the session back to your home network automatically. The story requires only one of relay, VPN or port-forward, and two are documented, but each is covered in a single sentence. Missing for 10: step-by-step setup docs for the VPN and port-forward paths (ports, router configuration), any relay option (Sill states there is no server), and independent or hands-on corroboration that remote access works.

support.subject: As a power user, I can reach my machine away from home, with the relay, VPN, or port-forward path documented

citations.quote: Remote Access lets you use your Mac away from home, through your own VPN, such as Tailscale, or through a port you forward on your router.
Away from home, Sill starts at a quality a slower connection can carry, and when you get home, the session moves to your network by itself.
